value.body: A production engineer runs and improves manufacturing lines so products are made on time, at the planned cost and to quality. Automotive, engineering goods, consumer-goods and process manufacturers hire them. A day involves supervising shifts, solving line problems, tracking output and working on process improvements.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. in Mechanical, Production or Industrial

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Shift supervision is common at entry

items.label: People engaged in surveyed factories
items.note: Up ~6% from ~1.84 crore in 2022-23; all factory jobs, not only engineers
items.source: MoSPI, Annual Survey of Industries 2023-24 (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as graduate engineer trainees through campus placement at manufacturing companies, or through GATE scores for PSUs. Diploma holders often enter as supervisors and grow with experience.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading engineering drawings and process sheets
Tracking output, scrap and downtime data

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is on the shop floor, usually in shifts.
Common next roles: production in-charge, plant or operations manager, industrial engineering roles.
Manufacturing hubs are concentrated in specific industrial regions.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
